newsitem.title: UK: Enviromed sees victory in board tussle.
newsitem.headline: Enviromed sees victory in board tussle.

text.p: Healthcare group Enviromed Plc said on Thursday it was confident of defeating an attempt by major shareholders to replace its board at an extraordinary meeting on January 17.

Managing director Thomas Murphy, who was singled out for attack earlier on Thursday by Enviromed's biggest shareholder Selfcare Inc, told Reuters that Selfcare was attempting to take over Enviromed by the back door.
"If you want control of a Plc you should make a proper bid," Murphy said.
Selfcare, which controls nearly 29 percent of Enviromed, said it had the support of BIB Holdings (Bermuda) Ltd, which holds a further eight percent.

Murphy, who has been at the helm of the specialst enzyme and diagnostics group since December 1994, said he had received messages of support from other shareholders and would be contacting more in the next few days.
"We are confident that we will win the day," Murphy said.
In his letter, Zwanziger accused Murphy of presiding over a collapse in Enviromed's value since he took the helm in December 1994, when Enviromed shares were worth around 112 pence.

The shares, which touched a low of 14 pence in October 1995, closed at 25 pence each on Thursday. Murphy blamed the collapse in profitability, which precipitated the plunge in Enviromed's value, on provisions needed to cover problems created before his arrival.

He said prospects for the loss-making group were good, and predicted break-even in late 1997 and a return to profitability in 1998. Enviromed produces enzymes for diagnostic and research use. It is also devising ways of detecting heavy metals in entities such as water, blood and earth and for tracing microbial contamination in UHT milk.
Enviromed said most of its shares are owned by institutions, including Britain's Equitable Life Assurance Society.
